newsitem.title: USA: Florida rescuer dies after pulling neighbors to safety.
newsitem.headline: Florida rescuer dies after pulling neighbors to safety.

text.p: A retired firefighter died from a heart attack just after rescuing two neighbours from dangerous surf, police said Wednesday.
Robert Brown, 64, had been exercising in his condominium pool and was relaxing on his fifth-floor balcony when he heard two neighbours -- Jennifer and Don Fulton -- calling for help.

The two were struggling in rough surf about 100 yards off-shore. Brown and another neighbour, Leo Kranellas, raced downstairs, grabbed life preservers from the pool and ran for the shore. A bad shoulder kept Kranellas on shore, but Brown swam out and helped the Fultons back to dry land.

After the rescue, Brown joked that he could not let the Fultons drown because they were good tennis partners, said Jane Craigie, another neighbour. But he suddenly collapsed and paramedics were unable to revive him. He was pronounced dead.
Brown moved to Florida's East Coast after retiring as a firefighter in Rhode Island, said Brevard County sheriff's Sgt. Bob Leatherow.
